text:
Error tracking is now wired into the app. The server booted cleanly with no errors, but I didn't send a real error to GlitchTip.

GBrain's notes say the team self-hosts GlitchTip at `https://errors.larkfield.example`. They dropped Sentry on 2026-10-28 because of event-volume cost. So I used the Sentry-compatible SDK (`@sentry/node`) and pointed it at GlitchTip, not at Sentry's hosted service.

- **`src/instrument.js` (new):** initializes the SDK from the `GLITCHTIP_DSN` environment variable. If that variable is unset, as in local dev, the SDK does nothing. Performance tracing is off (`tracesSampleRate: 0`) to keep event volume down.
- **`src/server.js`:** `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` is registered after the routes. Express 5 passes rejected promises from async handlers to it, so errors from the DB-backed route are captured.
- **`package.json`:** `npm start` now runs `node --import ./src/instrument.js src/server.js`, so the SDK loads before the app. I also added the `@sentry/node` dependency.

**Before it reports anything:**
- Set `GLITCHTIP_DSN` in staging and production. I haven't seen the DSN, so you'll need to take it from the GlitchTip project settings.
- Check that any other way you start the app, such as a Dockerfile or process manager, also uses `--import ./src/instrument.js`.

I didn't touch the Node version, since CI is pinned to Node 22.11.
